title: Short XLE — Energy Thesis Breaking on Iran Peace Headlines
entry: Short on bounce to $59-$60 (mean-reversion entry after Wednesday's selloff). Avoid initiating on continued momentum down — wait for one positive oil session for cleaner entry.
stop_loss: $62 daily close — implies WTI back above $103 on confirmed Iran escalation
targets: $52 — Iran ceasefire holds + Saudi production normalizes, -10%
$48 — WTI to $80, energy capex cycle peak narrative, -17%
catalyst: WTI fell ~5% Wednesday to $98 — first sub-$100 close since early May on Middle East peace deal hopes. Trump publicly toggling 'ceasefire on life support' language but headlines lean toward de-escalation in next 2-3 weeks. XLE has been priced for $105-$110 sustained WTI; sub-$100 breaks the structural energy thesis.
thesis: This is a tactical countertrend short, not a structural call. The energy sector has been priced for the Iran war continuing indefinitely — WTI sustainably above $100, refiner margins expanded, oil majors' capex cycles ramping. Wednesday's 5% WTI drop signals the market is pricing in some non-zero probability of ceasefire/de-escalation. If that probability rises to 50%+ over the next 2-4 weeks (Trump's stated 'life support' is rhetoric, but back-channel negotiations are ongoing), WTI mean-reverts to $85-$90. At those levels, XLE has 8-12% downside. Critically: this is sized SMALL (2%) and stopped TIGHT ($62) because the Iran war could re-escalate overnight with a single missile launch. The trade is asymmetric *only* if you respect the stop — the upside on a peace deal is 10-15%, the downside on a re-escalation is unlimited (XLE could hit $70-$75 on Hormuz blockade). Better expressed as a put spread (long $58 puts, short $52 puts) to cap the tail risk if you can structure options.
bull_case: Iran-Israel formal ceasefire announced within 2-3 weeks (back-channel negotiations succeed); Hormuz fully reopens; Saudi raises production to capture market share. WTI to $80; XLE to $48-$52. Refiners get crushed; integrated oil majors (XOM, CVX) trim capex guidance; sector multiple compresses from 14x to 10x forward earnings.
bear_case: Iran-Israel war re-escalates — single missile attack on Hormuz oil tanker triggers full blockade; WTI gaps to $130 overnight; XLE to $70+ in 24 hours. Tail risk: 25%+ adverse move on a single news event. This is why position sizing is tiny.
invalidation: Daily close above $62, OR Hormuz blockade event reported
